system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

ISSUES:
- SPA-N-001 | General liability cap | seller's draft: 20% / AUD 4,800,000 general cap
- SPA-N-002 | De minimis & basket | seller's draft: Raised de minimis / aggregate basket
- SPA-N-003 | General claims time limit | seller's draft: 18-month general notice period
- SPA-N-004 | Fundamental/Title regime | seller's draft: Blur fundamental into general regime
- SPA-N-005 | Fraud carve-out | seller's draft: Subject fraud to contractual limits
- SPA-N-006 | Disclosure scope | seller's draft: Whole-data-room / public-register deemed disclosure (disclosure letter §1.1-1.2)
- SPA-N-007 | Buyer knowledge qualifier | seller's draft: Blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion
- SPA-N-008 | Bluefen consent | seller's draft: Consent treated as obtained on delivery; ~AUD 3,600,000 (30% FY26 rev). AUD 75k payment unverified.
- SPA-N-009 | Riverlark facility | seller's draft: Post-completion release acceptable; ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding
- SPA-N-010 | Employee bonuses | seller's draft: AUD 420,000 closing bonuses excluded from funds flow (DD-005)
- SPA-N-011 | Ironquay IP indemnity | seller's draft: Narrow indemnity; DD-004/DD-010 AUD 180,000 open, SOW3 transfer conditioned on payment
- SPA-N-012 | Export/privacy incident | seller's draft: DD-006 incident, ~1,240 records to unintended address; preliminary
- SPA-N-013 | Sandbar renewals | seller's draft: Three renewals AUD 110,000 each = AUD 330,000 aggregate
- SPA-N-014 | Category separation | seller's draft: General regime overriding specific categories
- SPA-N-015 | Title verification | seller's draft: DD-012 share register offered as proof of title
- SPA-N-016 | Tax/IP open terms | seller's draft: Assume resolved / unlimited or general treatment

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
The Seller’s “market standard”, “agreed” and “FINAL” assertions are not evidence of Buyer approval. Below are proposed Buyer positions—not verified market benchmarks. The underlying SPA and DD documents have not been supplied, so factual conclusions remain subject to verification.

| Issue | Seller’s position | What Buyer should want | Recommendation and one-line reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| **SPA-N-001: General liability cap** | 20% of price: **AUD 4.8m**. | A higher general cap, with separate protection for fundamental warranties, tax, specific indemnities and fraud. | **Counter at 50% (AUD 12m)** as an opening position; unresolved risks do not justify accepting a blanket AUD 4.8m exposure ceiling. |
| **SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket** | Claims must exceed **AUD 25,000**; **AUD 250,000 deductible basket**, recovering only the excess. | Lower thresholds, a tipping basket and aggregation of related claims; no thresholds for protected categories. | **Propose AUD 10,000 de minimis and AUD 120,000 tipping basket**; the proposed deductible leaves substantial warranty loss with Buyer. |
| **SPA-N-003: General claims time limit** | Notice within **18 months**; limitations extend to all Claims unless expressly excluded. | At least **24 months** for general warranties, longer category-specific periods, and preservation of timely notified claims. | **Counter at 24 months and reject universal application**; Buyer needs adequate post-Completion detection time without prematurely barring other remedies. |
| **SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime** | Capacity and title share the general cap and time limit. | Separate fundamental warranties covering capacity, ownership, valid issuance and unencumbered transfer of all shares. | **Require a 100%-of-price cap, no thresholds and a longer period—propose seven years, checked against execution form and applicable law**; defects threaten the entire acquisition, not merely operating value. |
| **SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out** | Limitations, exclusive remedies and non-reliance cover all Claims; no express fraud exception supplied. | Express preservation of remedies for Seller fraud, fraudulent misrepresentation and fraudulent concealment, with appropriate attribution. | **Carve fraud out of all contractual restrictions, releases and non-reliance provisions**; Seller must not contractually shield its own fraud. |
| **SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope** | Blanket disclosure of data-room contents, referenced material, Accounts, registers and public records. | Specific, sufficiently detailed fair disclosure against identified warranties; a fixed, accessible disclosure record. | **Reject blanket deemed disclosure and require warranty-linked disclosures explaining nature and scope**; document availability alone should not transfer unidentified risks to Buyer. |
| **SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier** | No claim for matters known to Buyer or advisers, including anything discoverable from the data room or public records. | No knowledge exclusion; alternatively, narrowly defined actual knowledge of named Buyer personnel. | **Delete; fallback excludes constructive, imputed and adviser knowledge and imposes no enquiry duty**; “discoverable” would substantially neutralise warranty protection. |
| **SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent** | Reasonable endeavours; consent condition satisfied on delivery of written consent. No final consent or evidence of satisfied conditions disclosed. | A Completion condition requiring effective consent and satisfaction of clause 11.3 conditions, without unacceptable commercial changes. | **Require consent and evidence of fulfilled conditions before Completion, waivable only by Buyer**; approximately 30% of FY26 revenue depends on this relationship. |
| **SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility** | Approximately **AUD 3.2m** outstanding; security release follows Completion. | Verified payout, repayment and effective release of security and relevant guarantees at Completion, reflected in debt-free/cash-free mechanics. | **Require an agreed lender payout/release mechanism at Completion, with controlled subsequent registration steps only**; Buyer should not acquire continuing secured-debt exposure or pay twice for repayment. |
| **SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses** | **AUD 420,000** conditional Completion bonuses omitted from funds flow; on-costs unspecified. | Seller-funded bonuses and applicable payroll tax, superannuation and other on-costs, correctly treated under the price mechanics. | **Quantify and include these liabilities in funds flow/debt-like adjustments, with an indemnity for shortfalls and no double counting**; omission could leave Buyer funding Seller’s transaction costs. |
| **SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity** | Indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment; **AUD 180,000** recorded open, without bank verification, receipt or confirmatory assignment. | Verified payment and effective ownership of all relevant deliverables, plus protection against resulting title defects, claims and remediation costs. | **Require payment/title evidence and confirmatory assignment where needed, backed by a broader standalone indemnity**; paying the recorded fee alone may not establish complete IP ownership or cover consequential exposure. |
| **SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident** | Preliminary, allegedly immaterial export matter; access, scope, notification duties and loss remain unknown. | Prompt investigation, containment, evidence preservation, legal assessment and required notifications, plus protection against pre-Completion incident liabilities. | **Require investigation milestones and a specific indemnity for legally recoverable losses and response costs, with escrow considered once exposure is assessed**; uncertainty is not evidence of immateriality, but neither establishes a confirmed notifiable breach. |
| **SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals** | Three **AUD 110,000** renewals treated as ordinary-course operating costs. | Assessment of the **AUD 330,000 aggregate**, timing, scope, enforceability, termination rights, accruals and ordinary-course status. | **Review the related commitments together and apply consent covenants or price treatment only as supported by the facts**; neither ordinary-course status nor debt-like treatment is established. |
| **SPA-N-014: Category separation** | General limitations, exclusive remedies and non-reliance apply to every Claim. | Expressly separate regimes for general warranties, fundamentals, tax, specific indemnities, covenants and price/payment obligations, with overriding fraud protection. | **Insert a claim-category matrix and precedence clause across clauses 9.3, 12, 13 and 20.5**; a global limitation must not silently defeat negotiated special protections. |
| **SPA-N-015: Title verification** | DD-012 share register records Seller as holder of 100%. | Verification of legal and beneficial ownership, capitalisation, encumbrances, options and competing rights, plus valid transfer documentation. | **Reconcile the register with issuance/transfer records, constitution, relevant searches and releases, supported by fundamental warranties**; the register is important evidence, not complete verification of clean title. |
| **SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms** | Tax and IP warranties said to be settled under the general regime. | A separate pre-Completion tax indemnity and tailored tax periods; robust IP warranties covering ownership, licences, infringement and developer assignments, alongside the Ironquay indemnity. | **Keep both expressly open: negotiate tax-specific caps, exclusions and assessment-linked survival, and risk-based IP protection**; Seller’s assertion of settlement does not resolve distinct tax and core-asset exposures. |

**Immediate priorities:** Bluefen’s effective consent, Riverlark’s Completion discharge, bonus funding and Ironquay ownership evidence. These require closing solutions—not merely disclosure or capped warranty recourse.
=== END ADVICE ===
